title: CHAPTER 4: MEMORY AND FORGETTING
content:
👋 ሰላም፤ ጤና ይስጥልን ውድ የEthioFresh ተማሪዎች! ዛሬ የGeneral Psychology (Psyc 1011) Chapter 4 የመጀመሪያውን ክፍል (Part 1) በዝርዝርና በሰፊው ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል። በዚህ ክፍል Memory ምንድን ነው? Three Memory Processes (Encoding, Storage, Retrieval)፣ Stages of Memory (Sensory, Short-Term, Long-Term)፣ Serial Position Effect እንዲሁም Factors Affecting Memory የሚሉትን ዋና ዋና ርዕሶች ፈተና ላይ 100% ውጤታማ የሚያደርጋችሁን ጥልቅ ማብራሪያ ይዘናል። እስከ መጨረሻው ተከታተሉን!👇👇👇


4.1. Meaning and Processes of Memory

Memory is the retention of information/what is learned earlier over time. It is the way in which we record the past for later use in the present. Memory acts as a blanket label for a large number of processes that form the bridges between our past and present. Intelligent life does not exist without memory; it provides continuity in place and time, allows us to adapt to new situations using previous skills, and enriches our emotional life.

To learn about the nature of memory, it is useful to separate the process (the mental activities performed) from the structure (how information is represented, organized, and how long it lasts).

Three Basic Processes of Memory:
1. Encoding: Taken from computer science, encoding refers to the form (i.e., the code) in which an item of information is to be placed in memory. It is the process by which information is initially recorded in a form usable to memory. We transform a sensory input into a memory code that can be further processed.
2. Storage: The persistence of information in memory. To be remembered, an encoded experience must leave some record in the nervous system (the memory trace) and be held/squirreled away for later use. It is the location in the memory system where material is saved.
3. Retrieval: The point at which one tries to remember to dredge up a particular memory trace from among all the stored ones. Material in memory storage is located, brought into awareness, and used.

ENCODING
(Forming Code)
Sensory Input		➔STORAGE
(Maintaining)
Memory Trace		➔RETRIEVAL
(Recovering)
Awareness/Use


Note on Memory Failure: Failure to remember can result from problems during any of these three phases. For example, if you encode information only as a sound pattern without meaning, there will be no memory trace of its meaning. If misfiled during storage, it might be impossible to retrieve even though it is still stored.

👉 የMemory ትርጉም እና 3 ዋና ሂደቶች (Processes) :
• Memory (ትውስታ/አእምሮአዊ ማከማቻ): ቀደም ብለን የተማርነውን ወይም ያየነውን መረጃ በጊዜ ሂደት ውስጥ አእምሮአችን ውስጥ ጠብቆ ማቆየት ነው። ያለ memory ህይወታችን ትርጉም አልባ እና የተበታተነ ይሆን ነበር፤ ምክኒያቱም ትላንት የተማርነውን ዛሬ ካላሰብነው አዲስ ነገር መማር አንችልም።
• 1. Encoding (መረጃን መቅረፅ/መቀየር): ልክ ኮምፒውተር የጽሁፍ ቁልፎችን ወደ 0 እና 1 binary code እንደሚቀይረው ሁሉ፣ አእምሯችንም ከውጭ አካባቢ በህዋሶቻችን (አይን፣ ጆሮ) የሚመጡ መረጃዎችን ተቀብሎ ሊረዳውና ሊይዘው በሚችል ምልክት/ኮድ (Memory code) የመቀየር ሂደት ነው።
• 2. Storage (መረጃን ማስቀመጥ/መጠበቅ): የተቀረፀው መረጃ በነርቭ ስርዓታችን ውስጥ እንደ ምስል/አሻራ (Memory trace) ሆኖ ተቀምጦ የሚቆይበት ደረጃ ነው። መረጃው ሳይጠፋ አእምሮ ውስጥ ተጠብቆ መቆየቱን ያረጋግጣል።
• 3. Retrieval (መረጃን ማውጣት/ማስታወስ): የተቀመጠውን መረጃ በምንፈልግበት ጊዜ (ለምሳሌ ፈተና ላይ ጥያቄ ሲመጣ) ከአእምሯችን ፈልገን በማውጣት ወደ ንቃተ-ህሊናችን (Awareness) አምጥተን የመጠቀም ሂደት ነው።

💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ "የመረጃ መጥፋት (Memory failure) በየትኛው ደረጃ ላይ ሊከሰት ይችላል?" ተብሎ ቢጠየቅ፡ በሦስቱም (Encoding, Storage, ወይም Retrieval) ደረጃዎች ላይ ችግር ሲፈጥር መረጃ ሊረሳ ይችላል ብላችሁ መመለስ አለባችሁ!


4.2. Stages / Structure of Memory

The cognitive perspective relates the human mind to an information processor, like a digital computer. According to the influential model by Richard Atkinson and Richard Shiffrin (1968), memory consists of three main structures/stages:

⟵ Retrieval ⟵
Stimulus➔Sensory memoryAttention
➔		Short-term memory (STM)Encoding
➔		Long-term memory (LTM)
➘ Forgetting➘ Forgetting➘ Forgetting


1. Sensory Memory (Sensory Register):
• The entryway to memory and the first information storage area.
• Acts as a holding bin, retaining information briefly until we select items for attention.
• Holds unprocessed, accurate representations of environmental information.
• Iconic Memory: Visual images, lasts for a maximum of 1 second.
• Echoic Memory: Auditory images, lasts up to 2 seconds.
• Most information decays rapidly unless given attention and recognition, which passes it to STM.

2. Short-Term Memory (STM / Working Memory):
• Holds the contents of our conscious attention. Also referred to as active memory, primary memory, or immediate memory.
• Used in tasks like thinking, reading, speaking, and problem-solving.
• Duration: Holds information for up to about 30 seconds without rehearsal.
• Four Main Characteristics:
1. It is active: Information remains only as long as it is consciously processed/manipulated (acts as a "workspace").
2. Rapid accessibility: Readily available like pulling a file from the top of a desk.
3. Preserves temporal sequence: Maintains info in sequential order temporarily.
4. Limited capacity: George Miller (1956) estimated capacity as the "magic number 7 ± 2" (5 to 9 items).
• Chunking: Grouping small pieces of information into larger meaningful units (chunks) to expand STM capacity.
• Rehearsal: Conscious repetition of information to prolong STM duration indefinitely.

3. Long-Term Memory (LTM):
• System used for relatively permanent storage of meaningful information.
• Capacity & Duration: Virtually no practical limits; stores information for days, months, years, or a lifetime.
• Declarative / Explicit Memory: Conscious recollection of facts and events that can be verbally communicated.
- Semantic Memory: Factual knowledge (meanings of words, concepts, math rules).
- Episodic Memory: Personal experiences and specific life events.
• Non-Declarative / Implicit Memory: Unconscious memory where behavior is affected by prior experience.
- Procedural Memory: "How-to" knowledge of procedures and skills (e.g., combing hair, using a pencil, swimming, riding a bike).

👉 የMemory 3 ደረጃዎች (Structures) :
• Sensory Memory: ከውጭ አካባቢ በህዋሶቻችን የሚገቡ መረጃዎች የሚቆዩበት የመጀመሪያው በር ነው። በጣም አጭር ጊዜ ይቆያል (ምስል ከሆነ 1 ሰከንድ/Iconic፣ ድምፅ ከሆነ 2 ሰከንድ/Echoic)። ትኩረት ካልሰጠነው ወዲያው ይደመሰሳል (Decay ያደርጋል)።
• Short-Term Memory (STM): አሁን ላይ በንቃተ-ህሊና የምናስብበትና የምንሰራበት ክፍል ነው (Working memory ይባላል)። ቆይታው 30 ሰከንድ ሲሆን፣ የመያዝ አቅሙ ደግሞ 7±2 (ከ5 እስከ 9 መረጃዎች) ብቻ ነው። መረጃዎችን በቡድን በማደራጀት (Chunking) አቅሙን መጨመር እንችላለን።
• Long-Term Memory (LTM): መረጃዎችን ለረጅም ጊዜ ወይም ለዘላለም የሚያስቀምጥ ሰፊ ማከማቻ ነው። በሁለት ይከፈላል፡
1. Declarative (Explicit): በቃል መግለፅ የምንችለው እውቀት ሲሆን፣ እሱም Semantic (የህግ፣ የሂሳብና የቃላት ትርጉም) እና Episodic (የግል ህይወት ታሪክና ገጠመኝ) ተብሎ ይከፈላል።
2. Non-Declarative (Implicit): ባለማወቅ ድርጊታችንን የሚመራ ሲሆን፣ ዋናው Procedural Memory (እንደ ብስክሌት መንዳት፣ ፀጉር መጋዝ ያሉ የልምድ ክህሎቶች) ነው።


4.3. Serial Position Effect

The Serial Position Effect states that when individuals are presented with a list of items to recall, retention of any particular item depends on its position in the list. When plotted, it forms a U-shaped curve.

1. Primacy Effect: Recall is best for items at the beginning of the list. Because STM was relatively "empty" when they entered, these items received thorough processing and transferred into LTM without competition.
2. Recency Effect: Recall is best for items at the end of the list because, at the time of recall, they are still sitting active in Short-Term Memory.
• Middle Items: Items in the middle are poorly retained because by the time they enter STM, it is already crowded, causing them to drop out before being stored in LTM.

👉 Serial Position Effect በምሳሌና ማብራሪያ:
• ለምሳሌ፡ በአንድ ፓርቲ ላይ በርካታ አዲስ ሰዎችን ብትተዋወቁ፣ የመጨረሻና የመጀመሪያ የተዋወቋቸውን ሰዎች ስም በደንብ ታስታውሳላችሁ፤ የመካከለኞቹን ግን ትረሳላችሁ።
• Primacy Effect (የመጀመሪያዎቹ): የመጀመሪያዎቹ ቃላት አእምሯችን ባዶ በነበረበት ጊዜ ስለገቡ በደንብ ተከታተልናቸው ወደ Long-Term Memory (LTM) ተሸጋግረዋል።
• Recency Effect (የመጨረሻዎቹ): የመጨረሻዎቹ ቃላት ደግሞ አሁንም በShort-Term Memory (STM) ውስጥ ስላሉ በቀላሉ ይታወሳሉ። የመካከለኞቹ ግን STM በመጨናነቁ ምክኒያት ሳይሸጋገሩ ይረሳሉ።

💡 Exam Hint: ፈተና ላይ "Primacy effect የሚፈጠረው በየትኛው የMemory structure ምክንያት ነው?" ከተባለ መልሱ LTM ሲሆን፤ "Recency effect የሚፈጠረው በምንድን ነው?" ከተባለ ደግሞ መልሱ STM ነው! ይህን ልዩነት እንዳትረሱ።


4.4. Factors Affecting Memory

Ten Main Factors that Influence the Memory Process in Humans:
a. Ability to retain: Depends upon good memory traces left in the brain by past experiences.
b. Good health: A person with good health can retain learnt material better than a person with poor health.
c. Age of the learner: Youngsters can remember better than the aged.
d. Maturity: Very young children cannot retain and remember complex material.
e. Will to remember: Willingness and motivation to remember help for better retention.
f. Intelligence: A more intelligent person will have better memory than a dull person.
g. Interest: Higher interest in the subject leads to better learning and retention.
h. Over learning: Experiments prove that over-learning (practicing beyond initial mastery) leads to better memory.
i. Speed of learning: Quicker learning often leads to better retention.
j. Meaningfulness of the material: Meaningful materials remain in memory much longer than nonsense material.

👉 በትውስታችን ላይ ተፅዕኖ የሚያሳድሩ 10 ምክንያቶች :
• የመያዝ አቅም (Ability to retain)፣ ጤንነት (Good health)፣ እድሜ (Age)፣ ብስለት (Maturity)፣ የማስታወስ ፍላጎት (Will to remember)፣ ብልህነት (Intelligence)፣ ፍላጎት/Interest፣ ደጋግሞ መለማመድ (Over learning)፣ የማጠናው ፍጥነት (Speed of learning) እና የማጠናው ነገር ትርጉም ያለው መሆን (Meaningfulness) ናቸው። ትርጉም ያለው ነገር ከትርጉም አልባ ነገር ይልቅ በፍጥነት አእምሮ ውስጥ ይያዛል! 😉
